whatWasBuilt.checkoutAdded: `actions/checkout@v4` with `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` in the `shift-traffic` job of BOTH deploy workflows. The dispatch asked which ref and why: on a workflow_dispatch run `github.sha` is the head of the ref the run was dispatched against, and the workflow file itself is read from that same commit, so workflow and script are one revision BY CONSTRUCTION. It is NOT the deployed image's commit and the comment says so - `image_tag` is an operator input defaulting to `latest`, so the workflow cannot know the image's commit from inside the run. The guarantee bought is workflow<->script, which is the one this check needs.
whatWasBuilt.exitTable: 0 clean / 1 violation / 2 did-not-run. Both non-zero codes fail the step; they are distinct because the class being live and the check not having run are different problems.
whatWasBuilt.oneTable: All FOUR live call sites (deploy-canary and post-shift, in both workflows) now run the one wrapper; the four copies of the case statement are deleted. The stale comment at each call site, which still described the CHECK's 0/1/2/3 table as if it were the step's, was replaced with the wrapper's own table - that stale mapping is what produced the incident.
whatWasBuilt.theMarker: Positive, not negative: the wrapper requires a result object carrying `service` AND `verdict`, in EITHER of the check's two report shapes (live `{predicateVersion, results:[...]}` under --json; --from-fixture one result object). Requiring `service` is load-bearing: `--check-divergence` also reports `predicateVersion` + `verdict` over a byte compare, so a marker of `verdict` alone would read a byte-compare as a service verdict (falsifier F9 pins that). No service verdict means did-not-run - a missing module, a syntax error, an uncaught exception, a usage error, an unreadable service, or a report shape the wrapper does not understand.
whatWasBuilt.selfInflictedBugRecordedNotHidden: An earlier draft of the marker required the live shape only and read EVERY fixture verdict as did-not-run. The harness caught it on its first run (F1: a child that printed `verdict: PASS` and exited 0 was reported as did-not-run). Both shapes are now named in the shipped file, because the next person to tighten that marker needs to know a too-tight marker was already tried.

windowsCauseAndFix.cause: NOT a shell-quoting accident in execFileSync and not `shell: true` per se. `check-tagged-revision-env.mjs` builds a quoted command string and refuses any argument failing its `SHELL_SAFE` guard (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_.:@/=+-]+$/`), and the standard Windows gcloud install path contains a SPACE (`...\Google\Cloud SDK\...`). Point `P279_GCLOUD` at the real binary and the guard refuses the binary's own path.
windowsCauseAndFix.capturedStderrTheDispatchAskedFor: `unsafe argument refused (shell metacharacter or quote): "C:\\Users\\cente\\AppData\\Local\\Google\\Cloud SDK\\google-cloud-sdk\\bin\\gcloud.cmd"` - carried as the refusal's `detail` on `{verdict: REFUSE, reason: SERVICE_DESCRIBE_FAILED}`.
windowsCauseAndFix.conditionDependence: With `P279_GCLOUD` UNSET the raw check also PASSES on this host: cmd.exe resolves `gcloud` through PATHEXT and the guard never sees a space. So the dispatch's 'on a Windows host the script refuses' requires an operator to have set P279_GCLOUD to the real path - which is the natural thing to do and which produces the failure. A fix that only changed the default would have missed the seat's case.
windowsCauseAndFix.fix: The wrapper resolves the binary itself and hands it to the check through P279_GCLOUD: `gcloud.cmd` on win32 (the shim cmd.exe, which is what `shell: true` uses, can execute; the extensionless Git Bash `gcloud` it cannot), `gcloud` elsewhere. A configured P279_GCLOUD the check would refuse is DISCARDED and NAMED ON STDERR with the substitute - overriding a deliberate configuration silently would be its own defect.
windowsCauseAndFix.observedOnTheLiveService: Raw check with the spaced P279_GCLOUD: REFUSE / SERVICE_DESCRIBE_FAILED. Wrapper in the same environment: `RESULT=clean`, exit 0, with the substitution named on stderr. Wrapper with P279_GCLOUD unset: `RESULT=clean`, exit 0. Live verdict for cortex-api at 2026-09-18T18:26Z: CLEAN, consistent with the hand check in the incident record.
windowsCauseAndFix.notFixed: `check-tagged-revision-env.mjs`'s own `gcloudBinary()` still has no win32 branch, so a DIRECT caller with a spaced P279_GCLOUD still refuses. See contradicted.

threeQuestionGate: WHAT EXECUTES IT: the `shift-traffic` job of the service's workflow (cloud-run-deploy.yml for cortex-api, cloud-run-deploy-smartsite-mcp.yml for smartsite-mcp), last step. Also `deploy-canary` in both, as the first check. Both go through `scripts/p279-tagged-revision-check.mjs`, which spawns `scripts/check-tagged-revision-env.mjs --json`.
WHAT TRIGGERS IT: a `workflow_dispatch` with `inputs.action = shift-traffic` (the job's own `if:`). Nothing on `push` reaches it by construction.

WHAT FAILS WHEN A TAG POINTS AT A REVISION MISSING A CREDENTIAL: the predicate returns FAIL; the wrapper prints `RESULT=violation - a tag points at a revision missing a credential the serving revision carries`, names the tag, revision and missing names, and exits 1; the step fails under GitHub's default `bash -e`. Nothing is mutated - removing or repointing a tag is an operator decision and the output says so.

IS IT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE CHECK NOT RUNNING: yes, and that is the change. Different word (`did-not-run`), different exit (2 vs 1), different text (the child's exit code and the last lines of its stderr), and produced by the ABSENCE of a service verdict rather than by one. The 2026-09-18 run is the measured proof it was not true before.

WHAT BYPASSES IT: (a) a hand `gcloud run deploy --tag` or `update-traffic` outside the workflow - no step runs; (b) the `rollback` action, which changes traffic and has NO P-279 step, so a rollback can leave the tag set unexamined; (c) a future live call site that copies pr-checks.yml's direct-call pattern instead of using the wrapper; (d) a `run:` step that discards the exit code, or `continue-on-error: true`; (e) editing or deleting the wrapper - it is a repo file, so whoever can change the workflow can change the check. All five are named in the wrapper's own header.
